title: Simulator: scenarios, the harness, goldens and replay
tagline: How offline runs are set up, judged, cached and compared, with no game and no keys
summary: This slice is the offline test bench around the simulated game. Scenarios run the real stack against the simulated world and pin what it does as golden traces; the harness hunts many seeded worlds and judges a change against master's cached baseline; soak and latency runs watch memory and the stack's own computing; and the replay kit runs her real recordings through any commit's perception and scores them against hand-checked labels.
details_md:
Everything here runs with **no game window and no key player**. Inside a simulated run that is enforced, not hoped for: entering `with Sim(...)` calls `fakes.patched`, which points `control.client`'s `submit`/`send`/`wait`/`cancel` (and the Lie Detector alarm calls) at the fake player, makes `maplehelper.win32.send_key`, the game-window functions of `gamelab.window` and `analysis.recordings.record` raise `SimViolation`, and refuses any write under the real `gamelab/lab`. The simulated world itself (`sim/world.py`) and the fakes that stand in for the screen, the clock and the key player (`sim/fakes.py`) belong to the neighbouring slice; this slice is how they are *used* to check the stack.

**Four ways a change is checked offline** (README, Checking a change, from 2026-10-28):

1. **Scenarios and golden traces.** `scenarios.py` holds 47 named set-pieces, all on Tree Dungeon, Forest Up North II (map 10002073): 13 trips (`nav_tree_*`), 33 hunt-loop or grinding runs (`loop_tree_*`) and one tour (`tour_tree_run`). Each builds the stack the way `gamelab/__main__.py` does, inside `with Sim(model, scenario)`, which swaps in a fake clock, a fake player and fake eyes and refuses to run otherwise. A run returns a *trace*: every key plan sent, every cancel and splice, every log line, the result, and what the world saw. Traces are deterministic, so `golden.py record` stores them and `golden.py check` re-runs every scenario and diffs: a refactor that leaves all traces byte-identical hasn't changed what she does. Each scenario also `expects` the behaviour it is there for (a hop, an arrival, a retreat within 10 s), and `tests/test_sim.py` checks those.
2. **The harness** (`harness.py`). A *policy* (`tour`, `loop`, `loop-grind`, `walk`) hunts for a fixed simulated time on many world seeds, under a *preset* (how noisy and crowded the game is) and any of 60 named `--world` switches (what isn't known of the game, or a rule of the stack switched off to price it). What each run gave is read from the simulated world, not the bot's own reports: EXP a minute, kills, touches, HP lost, deaths, falls, drops picked up, trip and rope statistics, over a hundred keys a seed. `compare` applies *the bar* seed by seed (the pass/fail rule: more EXP a minute on at least 8 of 10 paired seeds and none more than 10% worse, no fewer drops picked up, no more HP lost, no death, fall, portal or hunt stop); `ab` runs the candidate against master's cached results and adds seeds (12, then 24, then 48) only while a *headline* difference (EXP a minute, touches, deaths, falls, stops) is within 2 standard errors of the paired seed-by-seed differences, i.e. can't yet be told from noise.
3. **The baseline cache** (`baseline.py`). Master's side of a comparison is run once and read after: one file per seed, keyed by the commit's *code* (a hash of its tree under `gamelab/`, `gamedata/`, `maplehelper/` and `config.toml`, Markdown left out) and a hash of the run's arguments, the game data's stamp, the Python and package versions and the resolved `GAMELAB_*` environment. Only deterministic runs are cached.
4. **Replay** (`replay.py`, `replay_run.py`, `replay_score.py`, from 2026-11-02). The simulator's eyes give no pixels, so a perception change is checked on three lossless recordings of the magician grinding Tree Dungeon (R1-R3). A child process imports a chosen code tree's `gamelab` and runs its perception frame step over the frames exactly as the live service did, fed her throws and the drops the hunt asked for from that night's telemetry. It writes a compact per-frame dump, which is scored against labels kept in git (`tests/fixtures/recordings/<clip>/labels-v3.json`): spawn onsets, births, touches, monsters under her, which monster each kill was, her casts at the dead, other players.

**Long runs.** `soak.py` keeps the stack going for minutes (on saved frames, in the simulator, or against the real perception service in a child process) and fits a line to memory samples to find leaks. `latency.py` runs the harness's hunts while timing, with the real clock, each stretch of the stack's own computing between two calls to the game, without charging it to the fake clock. Neither takes a `--map`: both run on the harness's default, the first map (10000012), whose scenarios are gone.

**Determinism is the backbone.** `golden`, `harness`, `soak` and `latency` each restart themselves with `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` (so Python's set order is the same every run) and `GAMELAB_FIXED_STATS=1` (her stats as measured, not as `config.toml` has them); the replay kit instead runs its child with the clip's `GAMELAB_CHARACTER` and `GAMELAB_GPU=0`; worlds and policies are seeded (`POLICY_SEED = 7`), and outputs are made the same to the byte whatever the number of worker processes. That is what lets a reviewer `spot`-check two seeds instead of re-running a table, and lets master's numbers be cached at all.

**Where things live.** Golden traces and saved harness runs hold map-derived data, so they stay in the git-ignored `gamelab/lab/golden` and `gamelab/lab/harness`. The caches and the recordings are on the scratch drive (`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/baselines`, `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/golden-clips`). Every job that runs frames or many seeds goes through the CPU rules' wrapper (`bg_quiet.cmd` / heavy.sh), 2 workers while the user plays.

modules.title: Scenarios
modules.tagline: 47 Tree Dungeon set-pieces: the real stack against the simulated world
modules.summary: Each scenario runs one of gamelab's entry points (a trip, the hunt loop, grinding, a tour, a Lie Detector retreat, the safety stop...) built the way `gamelab/__main__.py` builds it, but with a fake clock, a fake key player and fake eyes over the simulated world. It returns a deterministic trace and declares what it `expects` to show. The harness, the goldens, soak and latency all run through its `Sim` and `run_sim`.
modules.details_md:
**The registry.** A scenario is a function decorated with `@tree(start, **kw)` (a wrapper of `@scenario`) that registers a `Scenario` in `SCENARIOS` under the function's name. Since 2026-10-31 all are on Tree Dungeon (`TREE`, 10002073). Today 48 are registered: 13 `nav_tree_*` (trips, rope grabs and misses, landings near monsters, the evade step), 34 `loop_tree_*` (the hunt loop and grinding: crowds, the detector's misses, the Lie Detector, the safety stop, out of darts, her keys, the stat window, rope tops, a wall's corner) and `tour_tree_run`.

**What a scenario says.** `start` is (platform, x); `monsters` is `None`, `"all"` (the map's spawns), a set of platform ids or an explicit list; `seed`, `hp`, `limit` (900 fake seconds by default, then `SimTimeout`); `noise` and `realism` are the world's knobs (`world.Noise`, `world.Realism`), `her` the character (`world.Her`; by default `her_on(map)`: the thief's `LEVEL_25` from `HER`, level 25, HP 774, MP 623, keys `SIM_KEYS_PET`, or `HERS`' magician `MAGE_32` when the process plays her), `attack` the stack's attack mode, `remembered` her key bindings as last read, `book` her damage book. `expects` is a tuple of (what, trace -> bool) built by small helpers: `ends`, `logs`, `no_log`, `happens` (the world's log), `sends`, `moves`, `check`.

**`Sim`: one run.** It builds the `Clock`, the `World`, a `FakeEyes` for the stack, the `FakePlayer` and a `Trace`, and a second `FakeEyes` for perception: a `SyncFeed` over `WorldStep(Senses(...))` with her Shape and the look band (`reach.LOOK_UP`, `LOOK_DOWN`), ticked by the clock at the game's 60 frames a second (`feed.GAME_HZ`) and taking a frame 15 times a second as the live perception service does. Every look and glance of hers comes from that feed. Entering `with Sim(...)` first imports all of gamelab (`_import_all`) so that `fakes.patched` can point every path under `gamelab/lab` at a temporary folder (`gamelab-sim-*`), replace `time`'s functions with the fake clock's and the client's `submit`/`send`/`wait`/`cancel` (and the alarm calls) with the fake player's, make the real key sender, the game-window functions and the recorder raise `SimViolation`, and guard every write under the real `gamelab/lab`. `guard()` raises `SimViolation` whenever the fakes aren't in place, and `hunter()` wraps `Actions.play` with it, so nothing built here can reach the real player or game.

**`Sim.hunter`** builds `Hunter` as `__main__` does, plus what makes runs repeatable: the damage book's fits made on the spot (not on a thread), her jump-attack jitter from `Random("jitter:<seed>")`, a stub phone push, `FakePetCare`, a listener telling the world which way each throw was meant, and `_judged` hooks that tell the world (changing nothing of hers) each throw's target (`World.aimed_at`) and each live monster her ledger wrote off (`World.live_taken`), for the harness's `at_dead_*` and `live_taken` counts. `navigator()`, `tour()` and `tour_stack()` (potion HP 0.45, a fighting navigator) complete the stack.

**Running.** `run_sim` calls the scenario's function inside the `Sim`; `SimDied`, `SimTimeout`, `PlayerError`, `RuntimeError` and `ValueError` become the result string `error: ...`, a `HuntStop` becomes its label; only `SimViolation` propagates. The trace collects the plans, cancels, splices, log, `world.summary()`, the world's log, the eyes' and frames' counts, the files the run wrote under its temp lab, and the feed's record. `unmet` lists what a trace fails: unless `may_die`, she must end alive and on the map (not through a portal, not fallen out), then each `expects`. `tree()` adds one more check to every hunt: no hanging on a rope throwing (the world's `refused` at most `NO_HANG_REFUSED` = 10).

**Factories for families of runs.** `_loop(minutes)` and `_grind(minutes)` run the hunt loop or grinding and return its report; `lie_detector(after)` sets `FakePlayer.alarm_at` and records where the world has her `RETREAT_S` after the sighting and every key played since (checked by `LIE_DETECTOR_EXPECTS`: on a safe place within 10 s, moves alone, a late retreat refused); `safety_stop`, `darts_stop`, `key_check_run` and `stat_run` do the same for the safety stop, running out of stars, her keys moved in the game's bindings window, and the stat window read.

**Set-ups, not lucky seeds** (2026-10-31): a scenario about a reaction to an event sets the event up (monsters hurt at the start via `Realism.hurt`, points left vacant, the Lie Detector 2 s in) rather than keeping a seed that happens to bring it, so re-rolled world draws can't take the event away. Each docstring records how many of seeds 1-13 (or 1-16) meet its checks.

gotchas: The code registers 47 scenarios (13 nav, 33 loop, 1 tour), as the README's layer table says, and gamelab/lab/golden holds 47 traces (loop_tree_ore_waits removed 2026-11-16).
A run that dies, times out or hits a player error doesn't raise: its result becomes the string `error: ...`. Only `SimViolation` propagates, so check `unmet`, not exceptions.
`SimTimeout` is a BaseException on purpose: a loop that recovers from errors with `except Exception` must not swallow it and spin.
`scenarios` imports `harness` at the top (for its presets and camps) and `harness` imports `scenarios` inside functions: the cycle only works because of that.
Scenario docstrings carry long seed histories (which of seeds 1-N met the checks after each change); the current seed is the decorator's.
Ten scenarios (SLOW_SCENARIOS in tests/test_sim.py) run only under `--slow`.

modules.title: Golden traces
modules.tagline: Record every scenario's trace once; check a change leaves them byte-identical
modules.summary: A golden-master check: `record` writes each scenario's trace to `gamelab/lab/golden/<scenario>.json`, `check` runs them again and reports the first difference per part. A refactor whose traces stay byte-identical hasn't changed what she does. Both can run on a pool of processes with output identical to one process.
modules.details_md:
**Commands.** `python -m gamelab.sim.golden record|check|list [names] [--jobs N] [--folder DIR]`. With no names, every scenario. Scenarios whose map data isn't on the computer are named and left out; if nothing is left, exit 2.

**Same environment every time.** `main` restarts itself in a subprocess unless `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` (so no set of strings iterates in a different order) and `GAMELAB_FIXED_STATS=1` (her stats as measured, so editing `config.toml`'s `[character]` changes nothing). It refuses outright when `GAMELAB_CHARACTER` names anyone but the thief (`_thief_only`): the scenarios are the thief's until the magician's come (the design's S6), and `record` would overwrite the thief's traces with her stats.

**Running on a pool** (`ran`). With `--jobs N`, a `ProcessPoolExecutor` of N workers, each made ready as the command is (`_ready`: scenarios imported, every map loaded), runs each scenario exactly as here and sends back its trace as the JSON `record` writes (`Ran`). The longest go first, judged by their recorded traces' file size, but results are yielded in the order the names were given, each once it and those before it are done; what a worker printed is printed in its place. So `check`'s output is the same to the byte whatever N. The README's timing for Tree Dungeon's 30 scenarios at the time: 411 s in one process, 265 s on 2, 135 s on 4.

**Diffing** (`diff`). Per top-level key of the trace (but `IGNORED`, the docstring), the first item that differs: for lists, the index and both sides shortened to 300 characters (labelled plan, log line, cancel, world event); for a plan, which field parts (sent at, name, events from which event, end_ms); for dicts, each key that differs.

**Exit codes.** `record` exits 1 when a scenario no longer shows what it's there for (`scenarios.unmet`), but still writes the trace. `check` exits 0 only when every scenario asked for ran and matched, 1 on any difference or missing trace, and 2 when nothing could be compared: a check that compared nothing never passes.

The traces hold map-derived data, so they live in git-ignored `gamelab/lab/golden`. A branch in its own worktree re-records them in its own lab; once merged, `record` is run in the main checkout too.

modules.title: The harness
modules.tagline: Seeded simulated hunts, outcomes read from the world, the bar and `ab`
modules.summary: Runs a hunting policy for a fixed simulated time on many world seeds, under a preset and any of 60 named world switches, and reads about a hundred outcomes from the simulated world itself. `compare` applies the bar seed by seed; `ab` runs this checkout against a base commit's cached seeds, adding seeds only while a headline difference is unsettled; `spot` re-runs a saved seed or two to check it reproduces to the digit.
modules.details_md:
**Commands.** `python -m gamelab.sim.harness run POLICY [--seeds 10] [--minutes 20] [--preset game] [--jobs N] [--map M] [--world W ...] [--costs coded|measured|measured-1366] [--cache] ...`, plus `cached` (a commit's cached seeds read, nothing run), `ab`, `compare BASE CAND`, `spot RUN [--seeds 3,9]` and `check` (the world's own logs agree with its summary in every scenario). The standard command in the README: `ab loop --map 10002073 --preset crowd --attack choice --costs measured --world zero-walls --world near-misses --world walkers --minutes 5 --jobs 2` (and `loop-grind`).

**One run** (`scenario`, `run_one`). A policy (`POLICIES`: `tour`, `loop` = the hunt loop, `loop-grind`, `walk` = movement only, as the live QA walk) is wrapped in `_safely` (the Lie Detector and safety-stop retreat around it, `HuntStop` ending the hunt) and made into a `scenarios.Scenario` starting at one of the map's ten start places (`STARTS[map]`, the seed modulo their count), every spawn on, `may_die`, `limit = minutes x 60`. The preset gives `world.Noise` and `world.Realism`; each `--world` name then replaces fields of Realism, of her (`HER_FIELDS`), of Noise (`NOISE_FIELDS`), sets a `start`, or lists `stack` switches: module constants of the stack set for the run and put back after (`aim-before`, `hang-2s`, `no-hang`...). Worlds in `LAST_WORLDS` apply after the others whatever the order given. Some worlds are scenes: `s1`-`s7` set her start and the other players' camps as live on 2026-11-05 (README, Where she hunts); `policy-each`/`policy-other` set `POLICY_SEED` from the world seed for the run. `--attack choice|skill|regular` gives the thief `ATTACK_HER` (her Lucky Seven key casting it at its MP, each star's damage drawn); `--grounds 23,...` cuts the policy's hunting grounds to those (`_only`). `run_one` also applies the magician's Magic Claw search when she is played (`magic.apply`), sets the fakes' look costs (`COSTS`), the feed's costs and `route.ROUTES` (`--ways`), records telemetry with `telemetry.captured()`, calls `scenarios.run_sim` and restores everything in a `finally`.

**Outcomes, from the world** (`outcomes` and its helpers). EXP a minute over the horizon; her kills and a rival's; HP lost, touches, hurt and evaded; deaths, falls out of the map, portals; drops picked up as a share and by worth (`looting.worth_for`), cash a minute after potions at the user's reference prices; idle stretches beyond 60 s (`IDLE_GRACE`); time and touches on trips, piles and waits; retouches within 2 s; rope tops; landings near monsters; attacks at monsters dead by then (`DEAD_BEFORE_S` 2.5 s, `DEAD_NEAR` 40 units); jump throws by why chosen; trips and evades; loot visits; the nav log's cuts, replans, misses and falls. `run_one` adds the run's arguments, a coverage tally of her moves (`analysis.coverage.tally`, 3-7 KB a run), the feed's record, turning and attack kinds. A safety stop or out-of-darts stop ends the run's time there and counts against the bar as a death.

**The bar** (`compare`, at least `MIN_PAIRS` = 10 seeds in both runs, paired by seed): EXP a minute better on at least 80% of the paired seeds (8 of 10) and no seed more than 10% worse; at least the base's mean drops share; no more mean HP lost; no death, no fall out of the map, no portal, no stop (counted on every candidate seed, paired or not). It refuses runs on different maps or of different characters.

**`ab`** (`difference`, `ab_next`). The base commit's seeds come from the baseline cache; missing ones are run in the base's own checkout by a filler script (`--fill`, `GAMELAB_BASE_FILL`, else `<baselines>/base.py`) with the environment the base's key resolved. The candidate's seeds run here through `cached_run`. For each headline metric (`HEADLINE`: EXP a minute, touches, deaths, falls, stops) and each `--metric` (a dotted key of the result), the paired differences give a mean, standard error and t, and a verdict: 'zero' (every seed identical), 'too few' (under 2 seeds with values), 'beyond 2 se' or 'within 2 se'. While any is 'within 2 se' or 'too few', it moves to the next of `AB_SEEDS` (12, 24, 48). Then the bar is shown (only shown), and both sides saved.

**Saving and repeatability.** Runs save to `gamelab/lab/harness/<name>.json`, the name built from the options (`_name`). `main` restarts itself with `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`, `GAMELAB_FIXED_STATS=1` and the character (`--character magician` or `GAMELAB_CHARACTER`). Pool workers run at below-normal priority so a perception service beside them keeps its frame rate.

modules.title: Soak runs
modules.tagline: Keep the stack going for minutes and fit a line to its memory
modules.summary: Runs the stack offline for a set wall-clock time (on saved frames, in the simulator, or against the real perception service in a child process) while sampling Python's traced allocations and the process's private bytes. After a warm-up it fits a straight line to the samples for growth an hour, and diffs tracemalloc snapshots by part of the code and by line. Not part of pytest.
modules.details_md:
**Modes** (`python -m gamelab.sim.soak frames|sim|feed [--minutes 10] [--seed 0] [--no-trace]`):
- `frames` (`soak_frames`): real perception and localization on the saved frames as fast as they go. Each frame is shown for `HOLD` = 30 looks in a row; every 5th look includes the drops on her platform, every 30th the whole screen; after each look the hunter's bookkeeping (ledger, drop store), the monster tracker (`Tracker.update`), telemetry and a glance; a throw every 10th look for the ledger.
- `sim` (`soak_sim`): the hunt loop in the simulator (`harness.scenario("loop", seed, "game", minutes=100_000)`), the next seed if a run ends first. It wraps `Hunt._book` (to reach the hunt at the end) and `Senses.look` (to sample at every look and raise `SimTimeout` when the time is up).
- `feed` (`soak_feed`): the perception service (`service.serve_saved`) in a spawned child process on the saved frames, at its hunting pace; a `ServiceClient` asks of it as a fight does: a look with her band every 0.1 s, drops every 5th, the whole screen every 30th, a glance between, events drained, a throw every 10th. It also samples the child's private bytes and CPU time, its frames a second after the warm-up, and per-state timings of its pass, look and whole-screen search.

**Measuring** (`Meter`). Every `SAMPLE_S` = 10 s it records (seconds, traced bytes, private bytes). At `WARMUP` = 20% of the run (templates loaded, threads started, caches filled) it takes a tracemalloc snapshot; at the end another. `report` gives, for traced and private bytes, the first and last values after warm-up, min-max, the means of the first and last third (steadier than two samples, since big looks come and go) and the least-squares slope in MB an hour; then growth since warm-up by part of the code (`part_of`: stack, simulator, other) and the `TOP` = 12 lines that grew most; and what the stack holds at the end (kills in the ledger, piles, EXP gains kept, telemetry parts and MB).

**Isolation.** Telemetry goes to a temp folder in parts of `PART_BYTES` = 1 MB so rotation runs too; in `frames` mode the hit log is redirected to a temp file; nothing is written under gamelab/lab, no key is sent and no window touched. `private_bytes` and `cpu_seconds` call Windows' `GetProcessMemoryInfo` and `GetProcessTimes` through ctypes (None elsewhere). Like the harness, `main` restarts itself with PYTHONHASHSEED=0 and fixed stats.

**What it found** (README, 2026-10-20): `frames` for 10 minutes, Python's memory 152.8 MB after warm-up and 153.0 at the end, +0.4 MB an hour; `sim` for 10 minutes covered 5.6 simulated hours, the stack growing only by the ledger's kills (about 100 bytes each) while the simulator's own plan and log lists grew 8.9 MB, which a real run doesn't keep.

modules.title: Latency of the stack's own computing
modules.tagline: Time every stretch of the stack's thinking between two calls to the game
modules.summary: Runs the harness's hunts while timing, with the real clock, how long the stack computes between two of its calls to the game (a look, a key plan sent or waited for, a sleep), grouped by the call that ended the stretch. The time is not charged to the fake clock, so the runs are exactly the harness's. In game this time comes on top of the looks' own.
modules.details_md:
**Command.** `python -m gamelab.sim.latency loop|tour [--seeds 5] [--minutes 10] [--preset game] [--profile FILE]`.

**How it hooks in** (`measure`). The fake clock is told of every call to the game: `fakes.Clock.mark()` when a fake call is over (the stack's computing starts) and `Clock.charge()` when the next one begins (the same hooks `--think` uses to charge computing to the clock). `measure` replaces both on the class for the duration: `marked` starts a `Stretches` timer with the real `perf_counter`, and `charged` stops it and files the stretch under the name of the function that called `charge` (`sys._getframe(1).f_code.co_name`): `_now` (a look of the fakes'), `send` (a key plan), `wait` (waiting for a plan), anything else under `sleep` (a sleep, a look or a glance: her looks wait for the feed's frames through sleeps). If the run's clock does have `think` set, the original hooks are still called, so nothing changes. Then it runs `harness.run_one(policy, seed, preset, minutes)` for seeds 1 to N and restores the hooks in a `finally`.

**The table** (`Stretches.table`). One row per kind of call, sorted by total time: count, median, 90th and 99th percentile and the longest (ms), and the total (s), plus an 'any call' row. The 'a key plan' row is the one that matters most: what a look's answer waits for before her next keys go out. Each seed's EXP a minute, kills and looks are printed beside it, and `--profile` dumps cProfile statistics of the whole runs.

**What it showed** (README): profiled offline on 2026-10-20 with cProfile on top, it drove the speedups of that day. After the physics and attack tracks, the hunt loop on preset game over 5 seeds of 10 minutes (6,094 looks): before a key plan p99 2.7 ms and at most 4.6 ms; the tour before a key plan p99 2.2 ms. The latency analysis of 2026-11-01 led to the harness's `--think-clock`.

Times are this computer's, with whatever else runs; the simulator's own work (its world moves only inside the calls) and the looks' pixel work (FakeEyes; `bench-look` times that) are not counted.

modules.title: The replay kit
modules.tagline: Her recordings through any commit's perception, cached per commit and scored
modules.summary: Runs a code tree's perception frame step over three lossless recordings of the magician grinding Tree Dungeon (R1-R3, 2026-11-02), feeding it what the live service took from outside (her throws, the drops the hunt asked for) from that night's telemetry. Each run is a child process (`replay_run.py`) per recording; a commit's dumps are cached like the harness's baselines; `score` (in `replay_score.py`) compares dumps against labels in git.
modules.details_md:
**Why.** The simulator's eyes give no pixels, so a perception change can't be judged there. The kit (ROADMAP item 5, 2026-11-02) replaces hand-built replay scripts with one command set, in the simulator's layer beside the harness (the analysis layer may import neither localization nor sim).

**Commands.** `run [CLIPS] [--root DIR | --commit REF] [--out DIR] [--range A:B] [--unpaced] [--jobs 2]`, `cached [CLIPS] [--commit master] [--where]`, `score [CLIPS] [--dumps DIR] [--base REF] [--labels v3] [--json FILE]`, `check A B` (two dumps the same to the byte, or the first frame and fields where they part), `bench [CLIPS] --base REF [--rounds 1]`, `feed CLIP`. CLIPS are R1, R2, R3 (`CLIPS`, the `Clip`s for folders under `GAMELAB_GOLDEN_CLIPS`, default `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/golden-clips`; 6.6 GB of 1366x768 PNG at 15 a second, kept as fixtures by the user's word). Every job that runs frames goes through the CPU rules' wrapper; a replay takes about a core and a half.

**The clock** (`clock`). Frames are stamped in wall time (summary.json's `from`, local UTC-8, plus index.jsonl's `t`); the perception service's telemetry names frame times on its own `time.monotonic` (a victim's gain, a touch's popup). `clock` finds the one offset that puts the most of those within 2 ms of a frame, over candidates on a 1 ms grid around the median. The README: 1793544509.301 s on all three (R2 106 of 107 within 2 ms). The step then runs on the service's own clock (frame 0 at `t0`), so its events read against the live ones directly.

**The feed** (`feed`). From the tour's telemetry: each `attack` record becomes a throw told when the record went, with its side (the record's own, else the fight's `stance` within `STANCE_S` = 1.2 s before, else her target's side by the last scene), its key `TURN_S` = 0.080 s later when her keys didn't have her facing that way (as `Actions.throw` taps the arrow first), and its aim (kind, x, platform, track). Each tour `scene` that looked at drops becomes an ask on the last frame shown 12 ms before it (her platform's, or every one in view if the look was wide; mesos only if her backpack was full). `how` counts how each was told.

**Trees** (`tree`). `--commit REF` runs a commit: `git archive` of its `gamelab/`, `gamedata/`, `maplehelper/` and `config.toml` under `<cache>/trees/<code 12>-<lab 8>/`, with this checkout's DLLs and this checkout's lab inputs (`LAB_INPUTS`: calibration, name tags, character.json, the stat window's place, plate and pose models, map art), so both sides read the same; made once and marked `.ready`. A tree with no game data of its own reads `MAIN_DATA`.

**Running** (`run_one`, `run_all`). Each recording gets a `replay_run.py` child (`-B`, by path) in an environment with `GAMELAB_CHARACTER` set to the clip's character and `GAMELAB_GPU=0` (`child_env`); `jobs` run at once, polled every 0.5 s; a failure prints the log's tail.

**The cache** (`cached`, `key_of`, `_keep`, `data_stale`). A commit's dumps live under `<GAMELAB_REPLAYS, else baselines ROOT/recordings>/<code 12>/<key 16>/`. The key hashes the runner's own source (so editing `replay_run.py` remakes every commit's dumps), the feed, the lab inputs by content, the child's GAMELAB_* environment as the harness resolves it, Python and package versions, the recording's frames stamp and the range. The game data is checked rather than keyed: `key.json` names every data file the run read, by content, and a dump whose data changed since is stale and made again. A dump that opened a lab file `LAB_INPUTS` doesn't cover isn't kept. Labels aren't in the key: a score takes seconds.

**`bench`.** Pass times only from runs made side by side: base and tree alternated (base, tree, tree, base per round) on the same frames, paced, one at a time; never against a cached dump's times, since the machine changes between them.

modules.title: Replay runner (child process)
modules.tagline: One recording through one tree's perception step, as the live service ran it
modules.summary: The child process `replay run` starts per recording. Run as a script by path, it puts the chosen tree first on sys.path so that tree's gamelab is imported, rebuilds what the live perception service built (saved frames as the screen), and steps every frame at its own time, telling the step her throws and drop asks from the feed. It writes a deterministic per-frame dump and a side file of timings and the files it read.
modules.details_md:
**Importing the right gamelab.** It is never imported. `main` removes its own folder from `sys.path`, inserts `--root` first, turns off bytecode writing, and only then imports gamelab; it exits if `localization.feed` didn't come from the tree. An audit hook (`sys.addaudithook(audit)`) records every file opened under the tree's `gamelab/lab` and under the game data folder (both as named and as its junction resolves), so the parent can key the dump by them. With `--data`, `gamedata.paths` is pointed at another data folder before anything else imports it.

**What it builds** is what `service.screen_world` builds live, with saved frames for the screen: the map's model (`MAP_ID` = 10002073), her name-tag template from her calibration at the game's 1366x768 (`screen.NATIVE`), `SavedEyes` with the map's monster detector and minimap picture, `Senses` with her Shape (from `GAMELAB_CHARACTER`, set by the parent) and the look band (`reach.LOOK_UP`, `LOOK_DOWN`), and `worldstate.WorldStep` on the service's schedule. Then as the service tunes itself with a hunt attached that tells her throws: the hunting schedule (`service.HUNTING`) and `tracker.throws_known = True`. OpenCV on one thread, Windows' timer resolution at 1 ms. Older trees lacking a piece (the spawn watch, the whole-screen search, `HUNTING`, a throw's `aim`) are tolerated with getattr/hasattr.

**The loop.** Each frame is handed over at its own time in the recording (paced: wait for it with the real clock; the next frame read from disk in the slack after the pass, never during one); `--unpaced` runs them back to back. Before each frame, every throw told by then goes to `step.throw` (with its aim where the tree's step takes one). A frame missing from the recording (a gap: the game not in front) is stepped as not visible. Otherwise the frame's drop ask (if any) becomes a `worldstate.Asks`, and `step.step(runner.look(Frame(...)), t, True, asks)` runs. If the frame failed its checks, the eyes' recovery runs at most `RECOVER_EVERY_S` apart on the recording's clock (not the real one), so pacing can't move it.

**The dump** (`_Dump`: gzip JSON lines, gzip header with mtime 0 and no name, written to `.part` then renamed). A head line (format, frames, start, map, character, t0, throws, asks, the feed's hash), one line per frame, and an end line with the step's, tracker's and spawn watch's counts. A frame line, in map units rounded: `i`, `t`; `her` [x, y, platform, how, mode]; `v`/`vs` the view and whether registered; `bad`; `hp`, `mp`, `hpn`, `lv`; `m` the state's monsters (kind letter, place, platform, track, fading, facing, bar, box, score, picture frame); `tr` the tracks (id, state, kind, place, platform, fading, how, bar, gain, cause); `ev` events with plain data; `pl` other players; `sg` the spawn watch's sightings; `wd` the whole screen's detections; `loot` drops asked for; `say` what was logged. 0.28-0.41 MB a recording.

**The side file** (`--side`): per frame [i, late ms, pass ms, look ms, whole-screen ms, spawn-watch ms], the lab files and data files read with content hashes, the wall time taken. Timings never go in the dump, so a dump made twice is the same to the byte where the step is deterministic.

modules.title: Replay scores
modules.tagline: A dump against its recording's hand-checked labels, class by class
modules.summary: Turns a replay dump into plain numbers per label class: spawn onsets, births found, touches, monsters under her, which monster each kill was, her casts at the dead, and other players. `replay score` prints them per recording and in total, with a base commit's cached dumps scored beside from the same labels.
modules.details_md:
**Labels.** `tests/fixtures/recordings/<clip>/labels-v3.json` (26-37 KB each, in git; v1 and v2 kept beside): a version, the clip, and `classes`, each with an `about` and `items`. Frames are index.jsonl's `i`, places in map units, kinds as H/G/S.

**The classes** (`score` runs them all on one dump):
- **onsets** (`score_onsets`): the dump's onsets are its spawn watch's sightings grouped by (point, onset time), each at its first frame (`onsets_of`). `of_record`: labelled onsets the dump has at the same point and frame. `false`: onsets at no labelled birth (the user's zero-false rule: keep it 0). `refinds`: extra onsets of a birth within `REFIND_FRAMES` = 30. R1's `given`: newborns the state gave out as fading monsters.
- **births** (`score_births`): a birth is `found` by an onset at its point from 3 frames before to `FIND_FRAMES` = 15 after its first visible frame, split into those master's watch found and those it missed (where a fix's gain shows), with frames late and alpha at the first sighting (medians).
- **touches** (`score_touches`): the dump's 'touch' events matched greedily to labelled frames within `TOUCH_S` = 0.35 s: found, by popup, frames late (at 15 a second), damage number right, and false ones.
- **under_her** (`score_under_her`): at each labelled frame, or the one either side, a monster of that kind in the state, or a live, hidden or dying track, within `BODY_DX`, `BODY_DY` = 40, 40 of her.
- **kills** (`score_kills`): her gains' first and last bindings ('victim' events, let-gos removed) against the labelled victim within `KILL_DX`, `KILL_DY` = 40, 25; also the first on the victim's level. `strong` uses labels decided on the frames (`STRONG`: die1, frames, eye); `all` adds master's unchecked final bindings; unsure ones left out.
- **casts** (`score_casts`, only when the dump's `.feed.json` lies beside it): each throw's target is the track of its kind on its platform nearest its record's x within `CAST_DX` = 45, in the frame shown 20 ms before it was told. A cast at a labelled victim's track within `CAST_DEAD_S` = 1.6 s after its gain is a cast at her dead; `left_out` counts those the state had already killed (dead, or dying with a gain), which the hunt would have skipped.
- **players** (`score_players`): the state's player count against the minimap's red dots every 15th frame (more, fewer), distinct ids per 5 minutes, and of frames with a red dot by hers, those where the state has a player within `NEAR_PLAYER` (60, 60) of her.

**`main`.** Scores the dumps in `--dumps` and, if `--base` is given (or no dumps), the base's cached dumps (`replay.cached(..., make=False)`: it never makes them, and prints the `cached --commit` command if they aren't all kept). It prints a table per recording and in total (`total` adds counts, leaving out medians and late values) and optionally writes JSON.

**Master's numbers** (README, 40ba190, all three): onsets of record 244 of 244, 0 false; births 165 of 165 seen and 0 of 16 missed found; touches 71 of 71, 46 by popup; monsters under her 4 of 10; kills by v3 first binding right 123 of 151; casts at her dead left out 4 of 19.

flows.title: A golden check: does she still do exactly the same?
flows.summary: How `python -m gamelab.sim.golden check --jobs 2` re-runs every scenario and compares it to its recorded trace.
flows.trigger: A developer after a refactor, or step 2 of the README's order for checking a change.

steps.text: Refuses a non-thief GAMELAB_CHARACTER, restarts itself with PYTHONHASHSEED=0 and GAMELAB_FIXED_STATS=1, drops scenarios whose map data is missing and loads every map involved.
Starts a pool of workers, each made ready by `_ready`; submits scenarios longest first by recorded trace size and yields results back in name order.

In a worker: opens `with Sim(...)` (fake clock, fake player, fake eyes, lab paths redirected to a temp folder), runs the scenario's function, turns expected failures into the result string, and assembles the trace.
The scenario's function builds the stack through the Sim, as __main__ would, with seeded jitter and guarded key plans; every look comes from the SyncFeed ticked by the clock.

Loads each recorded trace, parses the new one through JSON as recorded, and prints ok, DIFFERS with `diff`'s lines, or MISSING. Exit 0 only if every scenario ran and matched; 1 on any difference or missing trace; 2 if nothing could be compared.

For each part of the trace but `IGNORED` (the docstring), the first item that differs, both sides cut to 300 characters (labelled plan, log line, cancel, world event); for a plan, which field parts: sent at, name, events (from which one), end_ms.

flows.title: Judging a change with `ab` against master's cached baseline
flows.summary: How `harness ab loop --map 10002073 --preset crowd ...` pairs a branch against master seed by seed without re-running master.
flows.trigger: Step 3 of the README's order for checking a change: a branch that changes what she does.

steps.text: Resolves the character, restarts with fixed hash seed, stats and character, checks the map and preset, and calls `ab`.
The base ref (master) becomes a commit and its code id: a hash of its tree under gamelab/, gamedata/, maplehelper/ and config.toml, Markdown aside.
Binds the run's arguments (`baseline.params`) and builds the base's `Cache` folder from the code and the key (arguments, data stamp, versions, resolved environment).
For seeds 1-12, reads the base's cached seeds; any missing are made by the filler script in the base's own checkout with `baseline.filler_env`'s environment.
Runs the candidate's seeds here (on a pool), caching each as it ends while the checkout's code is still as committed.
Each seed: preset and world switches applied, costs and stack switches set, `scenarios.run_sim` under captured telemetry, everything restored, outcomes read from the world.
For each headline metric and --metric: paired differences, mean, standard error, t, and the verdict.
If any verdict is 'within 2 se' or 'too few', go on to 24 then 48 seeds; otherwise stop and say why.
The bar is shown (not enforced) and both sides saved as NAME and NAME-base in gamelab/lab/harness, for a reviewer's `spot`.

flows.title: A perception change replayed on her recordings and scored
flows.summary: How `replay run --unpaced --out RUN` then `replay score --dumps RUN --base BASE` judges a perception change against her real frames.
flows.trigger: Step 4 of the README's order for checking a change: a perception change for the magician.

steps.text: Starts the recordings through the tree (this checkout, `--root`, or a `--commit` export), `--jobs` at once (2 by default), polling every 0.5 s; a failed child's log tail is printed.
For each recording, fits the clock offset (`clock`) and builds the feed from that night's telemetry: her throws with sides, key times and aims, and the drop asks per frame.
Writes the feed file beside the dump-to-be and starts a `replay_run.py` child by path with GAMELAB_CHARACTER=magician and GAMELAB_GPU=0 (`child_env`).

Puts the tree first on sys.path, builds the service's perception on the saved frames, and steps each frame at its own time (or back to back with `--unpaced`) with throws told and asks given, writing the dump line by line.
The dump is renamed into place at the end; the side file records timings and every lab and data file read.
`replay score --dumps RUN --base BASE`: reads the branch's dumps and the base's cached dumps (`replay.cached(..., make=False)`: never making them) and loads labels-v3 for each recording.
Scores onsets, births, touches, monsters under her, kills, casts at her dead and players for each side; `main` prints the tables per recording and the totals side by side.

not_done: The simulator's eyes give no frames, so perception changes are checked only on the replay kit's three recordings of the magician (R1-R3, Tree Dungeon, 2026-11-02, master 40ba190).
The scenarios and goldens are the thief's; the magician's scenarios are still to come (the design's S6), and golden refuses another GAMELAB_CHARACTER meanwhile.
Preset 'game''s values are guesses: nothing about respawns, other players or potions is measured (harness.py's own comment).
`--world near-misses-exact` (the frame step's exact finder beside the search, 2026-11-04) is measured on frames but not yet the default.

Scenarios that check an outcome still check one seed each; the proposal to judge them as a pass rate over seeds against master's, as `ab` does, is written up (D:/MapleHelper-scratch/sim-setups/classification.md) but nothing in the code does it yet.
Replay labels leave 14 kills out as unsure, and 87 kill labels are master's own final binding, unchecked.
Soak and latency runs are minutes long and not in pytest; their numbers are this computer's.
The CPU wrapper every job goes through (bg_quiet.cmd) doesn't pass on its command's exit code; the README notes a fix tried on a copy, the file itself left as it is.

The replay feed's timings are approximations: a turning throw's key `TURN_S` (80 ms) after its attack record, and the hunt's drop asks put on the frame 12 ms before the scene record that saw them (the tour's records carry no frame number). Both reproduce live's bindings and touches; neither is exact (README, Replaying the recordings).
